marble.name: Active and passive voice
marble.subject: English
marble.description: Use the passive voice to shift focus from the agent to the action or recipient, understanding how passive constructions affect the presentation of information in formal and objective writing
marble.prompt: When you wants to write about something without saying who did it — like in a science report — can they switch the sentence round to say "The experiment was carried out" instead of "We carried out the experiment"?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning the building blocks of writing — how to make complete sentences, use capital letters and punctuation marks correctly, and understand basic word types like nouns and verbs.

representations: Active/passive purpose cards (focus, unknown agent, formal report)
authoredAnswer: "The roof was damaged by a storm." (or without "by a storm"). "My lunch box has been taken." (the unknown agent is left out; has been + past participle keeps the present perfect). "The cake was eaten." is passive: it is the passive version of "Someone ate the cake" (was + past participle eaten). "The cake was delicious." is not passive: delicious is an adjective, and there is no active version with the cake as object

wrongAnswers.fix: Apply the two tests: is there a past participle, and can you make an active version? Try "Someone delicioused the cake" to show there is none.
